 Former Safari Restaurant owner Salim Said sentenced to 30 years for role in Feeding Our Future fraud case
 Eric Rasmussen & Morgan Reddekopp KSTP 
 --> 
 Feeding our Future sentencing
 Feeding our Future sentencing Convicted Feeding Our Future co-conspirator Salim Said was sentenced to 30 years in federal prison on Wednesday for his role in what prosecutors describe as Minnesota’s largest fraud scheme to date. He must pay $44 million in restitution jointly with other defendants.
 Said and Feeding Our Future founder Aimee Bock were both convicted on all counts after a lengthy jury trial more than a year ago. For Said, that was 21 charges, including conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering, conspiracy to commit federal programs bribery, money laundering, federal programs bribery and wire fraud.
 Bock is now serving a nearly 42-year sentence . Said received the second-highest sentence for the fraud case. Abdiaziz Farah was sentenced to 28 years for his role in the fraud case and 10 years for the attempt to bribe a juror during the first Feeding Our Future trial.
 RELATED: Feeding Our Future co-defendants Bock, Said found guilty on all counts in meal fraud trial 
 Prosecutors asked the court for a 40-year sentence, while Barry Zone, Said’s defense attorney, asked for 12 years.
 Zone attempted to separate his client from Aimee Bock, whom the government has called the “ringleader” of the fraud case. 
 “I’m not saying my client is an ordinary participant, but he’s also not the architect,” Zone said. 
 He also stated that he hadn’t heard of a single child who went hungry due to the Feeding Our Future fraud case.
 U.S. Attorney for Minnesota Rebecca Kline responded to that assertion, “This entire state and its taxpayers and people who rely on public institutions to meet their daily needs[…]Those are the victims here.”
 Kline also disputed the attempt to separate Said and Bock, noting that Said paid a bribe to her.
 In his arguments, Zone also detailed some of the trauma and abuse that Said experienced as a child in Somalia. He referenced letters written on Said’s behalf by his loved ones, stating that Said had been beaten and tied to a tree to see if the wild animals in the area would kill and eat him.
 But ultimately, U.S. District Court Judge Nancy Brasel said she had a difficult time tying Said’s traumatic upbringing with the greed she saw in his case, noting that he was employed and running a restaurant prior to the fraud.
 In a brief statement to the court, Said apologized for his role in the massive case, adding that he would never be in court for being on the “wrong side of the law” again.
 As she handed down the 30-year sentence, Brasel noted several aggravating factors, including the fact that Said has a prior fraud-related conviction.
 “You took more than taxpayers dollars to enrich yourself. You took the reputation of our state down with you,” she told Said after she announced the sentence.
 The case
 In 2020, prosecutors say Said enrolled Safari Restaurant in the Federal Child Nutrition Program under Feeding Our Future’s sponsorship.
 He then used non-profits and shell companies to open several other sites across the state with his codefendants.
 According to court documents, Said and his coconspirators falsely claimed to serve thousands of meals per day and are tied to $44 million in fraudulent proceeds.
 Said paid over $100,000 in kickbacks to Abdikerm Eidleh through his various shell companies.
 Prosecutors say Said used the fraud proceeds to buy a million-dollar home in Plymouth, a mansion on Park Avenue in Minneapolis, property in Columbus, Ohio, high-end vehicles, and went on several extravagant shopping sprees.
 The property and vehicles are subject to forfeiture .
 The other defendants
 5 INVESTIGATES analyzed the 32 defendants who have been sentenced so far in the Feeding Our Future case. We found that the median sentence was 38.5 months, while the average sentence is 76.5 months.
 Defendants who were sentenced to zero months received probation.
 Track all of the Feeding Our Future cases here.
